prerequisites: Physics 1: units of measurement, forces and moments in a plane, vector representation, graphical resolution of static equilibrium
Machine drawing: views, dimensioning, dimensional and geometric tolerances, bearing assembly
Mechanical technology: machining technologies, heat treatment of steel
Metallurgy: metal alloys and their applications, mechanical testing
Structural science: beam theory, mass geometry, de Saint-Venant theory
Rational mechanics: kinematics, rigid body dynamics, kinematic mechanisms, and force calculations

learning_outcomes.text: Know the basics of machine design.
Gain understanding of the many factors affecting the design of mechanical parts with special regards to safety and reliability.
Be familiar with design schemes and checks required to analyze machine parts.
Be able to design a mechanical part on the basis of suitable material and process selection, load analysis and functional requirements.
Be able to select from catalogues the main mechanical components found in machines.
Be able to draw and dimension the part for production.
Be able to critically analyze machines and mechanical components and to their functions and requisites.
Be able to clearly present the functioning of mechanical devices and the design issues involved.

syllabus_topics: Factor of Safety with Statistical Reliability Concepts
Tensile, Hardness, Impact, Fatigue, Fracture Testing
Metallic Materials (Steel, Cast Iron, Aluminum, Magnesium, Titanium Alloys)
Application of the Beam Model in Mechanics
Stresses in Contact between Elementary Bodies
teaching_methods: Numerical exercises carried out in the classroom
Problems proposed to be carried out at home with subsequent discussion in the classroom
Analysis and study of a real mechanical device by groups of students
assessment_rules: The examination consists of a written test followed by an oral test. The written test must be passed with a minimum score of 18/30 (or 17 with an asterisk for conditional admission). The final mark is the sum of the marks from both tests. For students under Module II (12 credits), assessment is a single final examination for Module II.
